_doc: LOCALE REGISTRY for asset-classification codes. Spec: prompts/JKR_SKATA_COMPLIANCE_LANE.md §PHASE-C
(2026-07-30). User directive: 'keep the code format pluggable via its locale json settings.'
WHY LOCALE IS THE KEY, not building or project: a classification code format is a JURISDICTION
artifact. Malaysia hands over to JKR/CIDB with SKATA+PeDATA; a US federal job wants Uniformat or
OmniClass; a UK job wants Uniclass 2015. The SAME building re-tendered in another country needs a
different code with the same geometry. So the format travels with the locale, and a scheme is a
reusable descriptor that several locales may point at (Uniformat is not US-only).
2. project_metadata key 'locale' in the building DB, if present
3. detect: match elements_meta.classification_system against each scheme's detect block
Step 3 is why an unlabelled building still reports honestly: Hospital carries Uniformat and is
recognised without anyone declaring a locale.
NOTHING HERE SYNTHESISES A CODE. These descriptors only VALIDATE and REPORT on codes the IFC
already carried (extractIFCtoDB.py §CLASSIFY). Absent stays NULL and is COUNTED.

_doc_level_naming: LEVEL-NAMING CONVENTIONS — a separate axis from the code, and the one our own fleet already fails.
These do NOT map a storey name to a code (that would be invention). They CLASSIFY the naming
convention in use so a model with two conventions in one building is a reported NUMBER.
JKR_extracted.db is the live test case: 21 distinct storey strings, and the prefix '01' names THREE
different floors ('01 Aras Satu', '01 Ground Floor Level', '01 Ground Level Floor'). Any level-code
checker that assumes the numeric prefix is a key is wrong on a building we already ship.

conventions.description: e.g. '01 Ground Floor Level', '02.5 Hvac Level 1', '02A Ceiling Level'
e.g. 'GROUND FLOOR PLAN', 'UPPER ROOF PLAN' — carries no ordinal at all

findings_to_report: conventions_in_use > 1        -> the model mixes naming systems
prefix_collisions > 0         -> one prefix names more than one distinct storey
no_prefix_count > 0           -> storeys with no ordinal at all
unknown_count > 0             -> storeys the extract could not attribute
